You are an adversarial verifier for a proposed STRUCTURAL refactor in the andesim repo at /home/nick/work/andesim.
READ-ONLY: do not edit, build, or run anything. Use Read/Grep/Glob only.

Claim (from reviewer plugin):
- file: qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c:559
- category: dead-code
- title: Unreachable kind guard in on_handoff_boundary; marker mode registers permanently no-op exec callbacks on EXIT markers
- detail: on_handoff_boundary (line 556) is registered only in pc_mode (line 632), and its HandoffSite is always created with kind = HYBRID_HANDOFF_ENTER (line 629), so the guard at line 559 can never fire. Relatedly, marker mode registers on_handoff for ANY matched marker kind (lines 646-653: hybrid_match_handoff_insn yields ENTER or EXIT per insn_match.h lines 24-29), and on_handoff (line 546) filters EXIT forever - QEMU1 exits(200) at the ENTER marker before any EXIT marker retires, so the EXIT-site registration plus its heap-allocated site is pure dead weight. Filtering to kind == ENTER at translation time removes both, keeping only on_handoff's guard if desired for the both-markers-in-one-TB case (which the ENTER-only registration still handles correctly, since the ENTER callback exits the process first).
- claimed safety: Exec callbacks never modify guest state; the EXIT-site callback body is a no-op today and the ENTER drain semantics are untouched, so drained state files and exit codes are identical in all three trigger modes.

Try to REFUTE it. For dead-code: grep the WHOLE repo (and the demo suite at /home/nick/work/andesim-demo, and consider that vsim lives in a separate repo /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim - grep there too if the symbol could cross repos) for references. For duplication: read both sites fully and check they really are behavior-identical. For stale-doc: read the doc AND the code it describes. For bug-report: check whether the behavior is actually wrong vs intended. If the change could alter ANY observable behavior (output text, exit codes, file layout, test expectations), verdict RISKY with the exact risk. If the claim is wrong, REJECTED. Only CONFIRMED when you verified the evidence yourself.

1	// Pattern recogniser for the magic handoff marker convention. The same
2	// predicate runs in two places: the QEMU TCG plugin (C) and the vsim PC
3	// pre-scan (C++).
4	//
5	// The markers are RISC-V HINT instructions: SLTI with rd=x0 discards its
6	// result, so it is an architectural NOP on every conforming core. Marker
7	// binaries therefore run unmodified on real silicon and on every engine
8	// (fast/cycle/hybrid) -- unlike the retired `csrwi 0x7C0` markers, where
9	// CSR 0x7C0 is MILMB on Andes cores and the exit marker enabled ILM at
10	// base 0, killing standalone runs. The 12-bit immediate carries the
11	// marker kind; rs1 is pinned to x0 so each marker is one exact 32-bit
12	// word. SLTI has no compressed form, so markers are always 4 bytes.
13	
14	#ifndef HYBRID_INSN_MATCH_H
15	#define HYBRID_INSN_MATCH_H
16	
17	#include <stdbool.h>
18	#include <stdint.h>
19	
20	#ifdef __cplusplus
21	extern "C" {
22	#endif
23	
24	typedef enum
25	{
26	  HYBRID_HANDOFF_NONE  = 0,
27	  HYBRID_HANDOFF_ENTER = 1,  // slti x0, x0, 0x5A0
28	  HYBRID_HANDOFF_EXIT  = 2,  // slti x0, x0, 0x5A1
29	} hybrid_handoff_kind;
30	
31	// slti x0, x0, imm: OP-IMM (0x13), funct3=010, rd=rs1=x0, imm[31:20].
32	#define HYBRID_MARKER_ENTER_INSN 0x5A002013u
33	#define HYBRID_MARKER_EXIT_INSN  0x5A102013u
34	
35	// Returns true when `insn` is one of the two marker HINTs. On match,
36	// *out_kind is set to ENTER or EXIT.
37	static inline bool hybrid_match_handoff_insn(uint32_t insn,
38	                                             hybrid_handoff_kind* out_kind)
39	{
40	  if (insn == HYBRID_MARKER_ENTER_INSN) {
41	    *out_kind = HYBRID_HANDOFF_ENTER;
42	    return true;
43	  }
44	  if (insn == HYBRID_MARKER_EXIT_INSN) {
45	    *out_kind = HYBRID_HANDOFF_EXIT;
46	    return true;
47	  }
48	  return false;
49	}
50	
51	#ifdef __cplusplus
52	}  // extern "C"
53	#endif
54	
55	#endif  // HYBRID_INSN_MATCH_H
56

1	// Translation-time capture of a handoff trigger insn. The QEMU TCG plugin
2	// allocates one of these per matched insn during vcpu_tb_trans and forwards
3	// the pointer as exec-callback userdata. compute_handoff_pc(site) returns
4	// the PC at which vsim should resume (i.e. the architectural PC immediately
5	// after the trigger insn retires).
6	//
7	// This indirection exists because qemu_plugin_read_register("pc") inside an
8	// exec callback returns a stale PC when V instructions retire just before
9	// the trigger -- TCG defers PC writes for performance and the gdbstub
10	// readback observes the lag. vaddr/size are deterministic at translate time
11	// (qemu_plugin_insn_vaddr/size), so vaddr+size is a lag-free post-trigger
12	// PC. Same predicate, two consumers: the plugin (C) and a doctest unit
13	// test (C++).
14	//
15	// Lifetime: sites are heap-allocated in vcpu_tb_trans and never freed --
16	// the plugin has no "TB invalidated" hook and trigger sites are bounded by
17	// the fixture's text (typically 1-2 marker insns).
18	
19	#ifndef HYBRID_HANDOFF_SITE_H
20	#define HYBRID_HANDOFF_SITE_H
21	
22	#include "hybrid/insn_match.h"
23	
24	#include <stdint.h>
25	
26	#ifdef __cplusplus
27	extern "C" {
28	#endif
29	
30	typedef struct HandoffSite
31	{
32	  hybrid_handoff_kind kind;
33	  uint64_t            vaddr;
34	  uint32_t            size;
35	} HandoffSite;
36	
37	static inline uint64_t compute_handoff_pc(const HandoffSite* site)
38	{
39	  return site->vaddr + (uint64_t) site->size;
40	}
41	
42	#ifdef __cplusplus
43	}  // extern "C"
44	#endif
45	
46	#endif  // HYBRID_HANDOFF_SITE_H

input.reason: Verified in qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c: on_handoff_boundary is registered only at line 633 (pc_mode) with site->kind hardcoded to HYBRID_HANDOFF_ENTER at line 629, so the line-559 guard is unreachable. In marker mode (lines 646-653) EXIT-kind sites get on_handoff, whose line-546 filter makes them permanent no-ops; handoff_drain exit(200)s at the first ENTER execution, so no EXIT callback can ever do work. Filtering to kind==ENTER at translation time is observationally identical (exec callbacks cannot alter guest state, drained files, or exit codes). The oracle exit-drain path (on_oracle_tick) legitimately uses EXIT kinds but is a separate registration branch that continues before the marker section and is untouched. Both callbacks are static; greps over andesim, andesim-demo, and vsim_andesim show no other references, and no test in tests/plugin/ depends on EXIT-marker registration in marker mode.
